description: We turn big ideas, like mission planning, risk, and resource limits, into something students can actually play. We're passionate about education, we're open to new ideas, and we value teamwork, creativity, and scientific accuracy. If you want to build something that inspires the next generation of explorers, you'll fit right in.
summary: Traditional STEM classrooms struggle to spark student interest and rarely let students solve complex, real-world problems. Research suggests digital games can help: a meta-analysis of 86 studies found a medium-to-large learning advantage over conventional instruction (g = 0.62) and that game elements designed for content learning work better than those added only for fun. Astronova: Beyond Evolution puts that evidence into practice. In this browser-based game, students command one of five missions inspired by real NASA programs: Apollo 11, Viking, the Space Shuttle Program, OSIRIS-REx and Perseverance. Each mission has its own mechanics and every mini-task, from building spacecraft and rovers to planning landings, installing instruments, collecting samples and analyzing results, is tied to a learning goal. Because decisions carry from one stage to the next, players feel how mass, power, budget, and risk compete instead of memorizing them. We developed the game using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, combining space-themed pixel art graphics. Our team has taken into account historical relevance, gameplay progression, usability and educational value. Our goal is to spark curiosity, promote learning in STEM fields and demonstrate that video games can be powerful tools for understanding real-world space engineering.
details:
ASTRONOVA: BEYOND EVOLUTION

Is a browser-based game that lets players live a complete space mission, from concept to operation, by choosing among five missions inspired by real NASA programs: Apollo 11, Perseverance (Jezero Crater), the Space Shuttle Program, Viking, and OSIRIS-REx. Each mission has its own objectives, estimated duration, and risk level, and players complete mini-tasks such as building spacecraft and rovers, planning safe landings, installing instruments, collecting samples, and analyzing scientific results. Decisions in one stage carry into the next, so players see how engineering trade-offs shape mission success instead of memorizing them.

Example

Apollo 11- The First Step To The Moon

Inspired by the historic Apollo 11 mission, this experience introduces players to lunar exploration and the challenges of operating on the Moon.

Players must prepare the Aurora lunar module, complete the necessary flight stages, and successfully land on the lunar surface. Once there, they must install scientific instruments and recover three regolith samples for further investigation.

Through this mission, players explore the importance of spacecraft preparation, lunar landing procedures, scientific instruments, and sample collection.

Five Missions

ASTRONOVA organizes its gameplay into five missions inspired by real NASA space exploration programs and scientific achievements. Each mission presents a historical context, a specific objective, an estimated duration, and a risk level.

The Game BENEFITS

ASTRONOVA benefits students, educators and anyone interested in space exploration by:

Making science interactive: Transforming scientific and historical information into hands-on learning experiences.

Introducing aerospace engineering: Helping players understand spacecraft construction.

Fostering critical thinking: Challenging players to make decisions and solve problems during the different stages of missions.

IMPACT

Our intended impact is to spark curiosity, strengthen STEM learning, and show that video games can be serious educational tools.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE OR SOFTWARE USED

We developed the game with HTML5 for the structure of screens and missions, CSS3 for visual design and animations, and JavaScript for game logic, interactions, and mini-games, working in Visual Studio Code. No special hardware is required, since it runs in any modern browser.

SCIENTIFIC INSPIRATION AND MISSION REFERENCES

NASA's Apollo 11 mission: Inspired the lunar exploration and regolith collection experience.

NASA's Perseverance mission: Inspired the Martian rover construction and sample preservation challenges.

NASA's Space Shuttle Program: Inspired the spaceflight and Hubble Space Telescope maintenance experience.

NASA's Viking 1 and 2 missions: Inspired the Martian landing-site selection and scientific investigation activities.

NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission: Inspired the asteroid exploration, TAGSAM sample collection, and sample-return experience.

Visual Design:

Pixel Art: Used to create the game's visual identity and space exploration environments.

Web-based interface: Combines dark space-themed backgrounds, neon elements, and interactive mission cards to create an immersive experience.
